items.q: men like Ted Lewis, Ross Garner, Lopez, Vincent Lopez, former jazz bands, who copied after the style of the original Dixieland jazz bands recording

ctx.x: Well, we forgot about Lytel and Frankie Signorelli. About 1920, Signorelli joined my band. At that time they may have had a Memphis Five, but I never heard of them stopping the machine. Well, I had a little bit of friction with Roberson. He had promised the band a thousand dollars if I put Margie over. Well, I saw the plug of Margie for him, sang it for him, placed it on the record for him, and after he got his first statement, he didn't say anything. I asked him about what he was going to do to three of them.…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-06-14
items.q: There was Ted Lewis's jazz band on Columbia, which was no more a jazz band than the Boston Promenade Orchestra.

ctx.x: Today is Sunday, June 14th, 1959. This is Brian Rust of London, England. I'm sitting in the living room of Nick LaRocca's home, 2218 Constance Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. Mr LaRocca has done me the honour of making a tape recording of his voice telling his story of how he came to create jazz and his opinions and the whole story of the growth of the music. And he's asked me to give my side of it, how I came to be interested in the music and what it means to me and to English people now. Until 1936, I'd never…

it's easy enough to listen to them. I've only got to listen to those and compare them with the original Dixieland Jazz Band to realise that the one is Ragtime and the other is Jazz. The original Dixieland Jazz Band isn't called Jazz for Nothing. There are other musicians having laid claim to having made the first jazz records.
